newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli cabinet approves budget cuts for 1998.
newsitem.headline: Israeli cabinet approves budget cuts for 1998.

text.p: Israel's cabinet approved the Treasury's outline for the 1998 budget in a meeting late on Wednesday, Treasury officials said.

Ministers voted to approve a Treasury plan to slash 2.3 billion shekels ($650 million) from next year's 164.4 billion shekel budget. The cuts aim to bring the deficit down to 2.4 percent of gross domestic product.
The spending cuts were strongly opposed by some ministers, three of whom voted against them. Nine voted in favour, while four were absent or abstained, officials said.
Cabinet ministers also voted to keep the country's inflation target at seven to 10 percent, the same level as this year.
In a separate vote, the cabinet unanimously approved with minor changes a package of approximately 100 structural changes to the economy.
Ministers gave their approval to two reforms -- imports of fresh produce and the opening of domestic airline routes to competition -- which they had earlier rejected.
